## Recently closed

### How should the native-source release gate be closed when rbit 0.2.2 pulls ring unconditionally?

`resolved` · `@templartorrent.question.ring-release-gate/2`

The strict native-source audit still reports ring 0.17.14 through rbit 0.2.2 -> reqwest 0.12 (rustls-tls) -> rustls -> ring. Inspection of the registry source on 2026-10-22 shows rbit's Cargo.toml declares reqwest with features = ["rustls-tls"] and no Cargo feature to disable it; reqwest is used in rbit's tracker/http.rs, webseed.rs and upnp.rs. The adapter uses rbit::HttpTracker for announces. Options: (a) keep rbit as published and record the gate as open in every release claim; (b) fork or patch rbit to make reqwest optional and announce over an application-owned bounded plain-HTTP transport, which also removes HTTPS trackers unless another pure-Rust TLS is chosen; (c) accept ring as a reviewed exception to the strict policy.

**Resolution.** Owner chose (b) on 2026-10-22: rbit 0.2.2 is vendored at vendor/rbit with reqwest behind an off-by-default http-client feature and applied through [patch.crates-io]; the adapter announces over its own bounded HTTP transport; https trackers are refused with a visible reason. See decision fork-rbit-for-native-gate and milestone native-source-gate.

**Resolved by** [Fork rbit 0.2.2 in-tree to drop reqwest/rustls/ring; announce over an application-owned HTTP transport](DECISION-HISTORY.md#revision-1--fork-rbit-022-in-tree-to-drop-reqwestrustlsring-announce-over-an-application-owned-http-transport) `@templartorrent.decision.fork-rbit-for-native-gate/1`
